SUBJECT: AMENDMENT TO CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL LISTED IN
PLANNING COMMISSION RESOLUTION NO. 2015-07 FOR CONDITIONAL USE
PERMIT NO. 817 REGARDING THE OPERATION OF A NEIGHBORHOOD
MARKET/CONVENIENCE STORE, LOCATED AT 10840 GARFIELD AVENUE (7-
ELEVEN)

PURPOSE: A request to consider “an amendment to the conditions of approval listed in
Planning Commission Resolution No. 2015-07 for Conditional Use Permit No. 817 regarding the
operation of an existing neighborhood market/convenience store, located at 10840 Garfield
Avenue (7-Eleven).”

RECOMMENDED ACTION:
1. CONDUCT a public hearing, pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Table 11.51-1 and
  Section 11.50.040 (B);
2. ACCEPT the determination that this matter is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act; and
3. ADOPT the findings outlined in Resolution No. 2023-08 (Attachment A).

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION: Advertising and notification of the public hearing for the
application was conducted in compliance with Chapter 11.50 of the South Gate Municipal Code.
Notice of the hearing was originally posted and published in the “South Gate Press” newspaper
and was mailed to surrounding properties on August 3, 2023.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: This project is Categorically Exempt from CEQA
under state regulations known as the “CEQA Guidelines” codified at Division 6 of Title 14 of the
California Code of Regulations. The Class 1 (Existing Facilities) exemption under the CEQA
Guidelines, at 14 CCR Section 15301, consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting,
leasing, licensing, or minor alterations of existing public or private structures, facilities,
mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use
beyond that existing at the time of the lead agency’s determination. The project qualifies under
Class 1 Exemption since the proposed project does not expand an existing structure or former use.

BACKGROUND: The Planning Commission approved Planning Commission (PC) Resolution
No. 2015-07 for Conditional Use Permit No. 817 on June 16, 2015, approving the sale of beer and
wine for off-site consumption for 7-Eleven, Inc. at 10840 Garfield Avenue. This 7-Eleven has been
in operation for approximately five years. The applicant has maintained the operations of a safe,
community-oriented business without adverse impacts on the surrounding community as a result
of the applicant’s adherence to the conditions of approval listed in PC Resolution No. 2015-07, the
corporate policies dictated by 7-Eleven, Inc. and State Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control
(ABC) policies and regulations. The applicant obtained a Type-20 License (Off-Sale Beer and
Wine) from ABC in July 2018. This license has been active since July 2018 without interruption,  9
 disciplinary history, or disciplinary action.

The applicant and attorney for 7-Eleven, Inc. are now requesting to modify a condition of approval,
listed in PC Resolution No. 2015-07 (Attachment B). Condition of approval number 20 states that
“Beer shall not be sold in units less than a six-pack.” The applicant’s request is to modify the
condition of approval to allow for the sale of beer in minimum quantities of three.

ANALYSIS: The existing neighborhood market/convenience store remains compatible with
adjacent properties and the surrounding neighborhood, as determined in Conditional Use Permit
No. 817. No exterior or interior modifications are proposed as a part of this application. Therefore,
this application is solely to modify the above-mentioned condition of approval. The applicant
proposes to modify the subject condition of approval as follows:

  20. Beer or malt beverages shall not be sold units in fewer than a six three-pack
  quantities.

This proposed condition of approval modification will not affect the overall operations of the
existing business as the sale of beer and wine falls within the common types of groceries that
customers expect to be sold at neighborhood markets/convenience stores.

Departmental Comments/Advisories
The subject application was routed to City Departments and Divisions for advisory input and
additional comments/requirements and conditions of approval. The Building & Safety Division
provided additional proposed conditions of approval to ensure the existing site is restriped for
parking spaces that may have faded over the last few years since the initial opening of the business.
The Code Enforcement Division similarly proposed additional conditions of approval to ensure
the site is maintained according to overall property maintenance standards. The Police Department
did not express concerns regarding the ongoing business operations and noted that calls for service
over the last year have amounted to safety alarm issues and loitering concerns, none related to the
sale of beer and wine at the site. The proposed additional conditions of approval are listed as
follows:

  Building and Safety Requirements:
  64. Under the direction of the Building Official and the Senior Building Inspector, a
  restriping of the parking lot shall be completed.
  65. ADA parking stalls and signage for said stalls must be maintained at all times.
  66. ADA parking shall be clearly identified, demarcated and maintained at all times.

  Code Enforcement Requirements:

  67. Maintain the site clean and free of trash/litter/debris/graffiti, including private
  property and public right-of-way immediately, adjacent to the business, pursuant to
  South Gate Municipal Code 5.08.020 (A).
  68. Establish a routine property maintenance plan.
  69. Maintain landscaped areas with healthful vegetation; keep free of overgrown
  vegetation/weeds, etc.

  10
 CONCLUSION: Based on the analysis provided above, it is the staff’s recommendation that the
Planning Commission approve an amendment to Planning Commission Resolution No. 2015-07
for Conditional Use Permit No. 817.

ATTACHMENTS:  A: Proposed Planning Commission Resolution No. 2023-10
  B: Planning Commission Resolution No. 2015-07
  C. Type 20 ABC License

  11
   ATTACHMENT A
  RESOLUTION NO. 2023-10

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF THE CITY OF SOUTH GATE, CALIFORNIA
  APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL LISTED
  IN PLANNING COMMISSION RESOLUTION NO. 2015-07
  FOR CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 817,
  AT 10840 GARFIELD AVENUE (7-ELEVEN)

  WHEREAS, on January 7, 2015, the Department of Community Development received
an application from 7-Eleven, Inc, for Conditional Use Permit No. 817 to allow the operation of a
mini-market (7-Eleven) with a Type 20 Off-Sale Beer and Wine license located at I 0840 Garfield
Avenue; and

  WHEREAS, upon giving the required notice, the Planning Commission did, on the
sixteenth day of June 2015, conduct a duly advertised public hearing as required by law to consider
the approval of said Conditional Use Permit. Notice of the hearing was originally published in the
"WAVE" and mailed to the surrounding properties on June 4, 2015; and

  WHEREAS, on June 15, 2023, the Department of Community Development received an
application from 7-Eleven, Inc. (“Applicant”) requesting an amendment to conditions of approval
listed in Planning Commission Resolution No. 2015-07 for Conditional Use Permit No. 817 to
allow the sale of beer and wine at an existing neighborhood market/convenience store, located at
10840 Garfield Avenue (7-Eleven);

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission upon giving the required notice, did, on the
fifteenth day of August, 2023, conduct a duly advertised public hearing as required by law to
consider the approval of said amendment to Planning Commission Resolution No. 2015-07 for
Conditional Use Permit No. 817. Notice of the hearing was originally posted and published in the
“South Gate Press” newspaper and was mailed to surrounding properties on August 3, 2023; and

  WHEREAS, studies and investigations were made and a staff report with
recommendations was submitted; and

  WHEREAS, on August 15, 2023, the Planning Commission determined that the facts of
this matter are as follows:

1. On January 7, 2015, the Department of Community Development received an application from
  7-Eleven, Inc. for Conditional Use Permit No. 817 to allow the operation of a Type 20 Off-
  Sale Beer and Wine license.

2. The subject property is located at 10840 Garfield Avenue, the north-east corner of Garfield
  Avenue and Imperial Highway. The General Plan designation for this property is Imperial
  District Sub-Area 3. The subject property measures approximately 13,500 square feet.

3. The 7-Eleven will operate 24/7, and alcohol sales will be in accordance with the provisions of
  a type-20 liquor license as adopted by the State Alcohol Beverage Control Board (ABC) from
  6:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. Deliveries will occur between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

  12
   WHEREAS, the City Planning Commission made the following findings:

1. The subject application will not be detrimental to public health, safety, and welfare or
  adversely affect property values or the present and future development of the surrounding area
  with the incorporation of the conditions of approval.

2. The proposed use is consistent with the goals and objectives of the South Gate General Plan
  because it will promote business and serve city residents.

3. Upon compliance with the attached conditions of approval, the subject use will not harm
  adjacent properties.

4. The proposed Conditional Use Permit is Categorically Exempt under Class 1(Existing
  Facilities) Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act. Class 1 consists of the
  operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing
  public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features,
  involving negligible or no expansion of use beyond that existing at the time of the lead agency's
  determination.

 NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Planning Commission of the City of South
Gate, pursuant to the facts noted above, does hereby approve the amendment to modify the
conditions of approval listed in Planning Commission Resolution No. 2015-07 for Conditional Use
Permit No. 817, subject to the conditions of approval contained in Exhibit 1. This recommendation
was adopted by the following vote at the August 15, 2023 Planning Commission meeting.

General Requirements:

  26. Right of the City to Impose Modifications
  Upon sixty(60) days prior notice given in writing, in advance, to the Permittee at a hearing
  at which the Permittee is given an opportunity to be heard, the City shall have the right to
  modify the terms of this conditional use permit, to impose such further and additional
  conditions to the conditional use permit herein granted that are reasonably related to crime
  prevention, crime protection, parking, traffic, circulation, safety, health, surrounding land
  use compatibility, noise, vandalism, poor maintenance of property, aesthetics and welfare
  at or in the immediate vicinity of the property which is the subject of this conditional use
  permit.
  27. Citation
  Any violation of the code requirements and/or conditions of approval may be subject to the
  issuance of a citation that could result in a fine as set by the Planning Commission, after
  notice, at which time the applicant may address the Commission.
  28. Revocation
  Violations of the conditions of this conditional use permit can result in the revocation or
  modification of this application by the issuing body at a regularly scheduled meeting,
  notice of which will be given to the applicant by first class mail, postage prepaid, or by
  posting notice of said hearing at two prominent locations on the premises to which the
  permit refers.
  29. Reimbursement
  The City Planning Commission may impose, as a condition of continuation, reinstatement

  16
   or re-issuance of any permit, a requirement that the Permittee reimburse the City for all
  costs and expenses reasonably incurred in the investigating, identifying, and documenting
  the violation and in processing information concerning the violation for presentation to the
  City Planning Commission, and upon appeal, to the City Council.

  30. Expiration of Conditional Use Permit
  This conditional use permit shall expire unless exercised within one year from the date of
  approval or unless a request for extension is submitted for Planning Commission review
  three months prior to such expiration.

  within forty eight (48) hours, with or without notice from the City, as a condition of the

  Community Development Department
  Memorandum

  To:  Planning Commission
  From:  Yalini Siva, Senior Planner
  Date:  August 15, 2023
  Re:  Item No. 3

In order to address ongoing inquiries regarding front yard setback area zoning standards in residential zones,
Planning staff is listing the existing Zoning Code standards below that may be amended to address residential
parking concerns throughout the City. Staff requests the Planning Commission provide staff with
recommendations to help address the growing concerns regarding in which the City will address the worsening
conditions of the lack of onsite residential parking. Staff will research the Planning Commission’s
recommendations for feasibility and will then return with proposed code amendments for consideration and
recommendation to the City Council.

South Gate Municipal Code Section 11.25.070 Residential operating standards:

  “The following operational standards and requirements shall apply to all residential units,
  buildings, and uses in all zones where residential uses are allowed.

  A. Hardscape in Front Setback. Hardscape (driveways, walkways, steps, terraces, and other
  site design elements that are placed directly on grade) within the front setback shall be
  limited to the permitted driveway and a six-foot-long access walk to the entry of the
  residence.

  B. Residential Parking.
  1. Parking of vehicles shall only occur within the designated driveway or garage.
  2. No vehicle or trailer of any kind for daily use may be parked or stored for more than
  thirty-six hours in any required building line setback area other than on a designated
  parking space.
  3. No recreational vehicle, boat, or trailer of any kind for occasional or recreational use
  may be parked or stored on a designated driveway.”

On July 18, 2023, the Planning Commission requested staff provide the Commission with a compilation
of regional and local front yard standards, in order to review the manner in which other municipalities
are enforcing or not enforcing existing or revised development standards.
